question: Where is the headquarter of Indian Bureau of Mines?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The headquarters of the Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM) is located in **Nagpur, Maharashtra, India**.
 
• The Indian Bureau of Mines is a government agency under the Ministry of Mines of the Government of India. It was established in 1948, primarily to promote systematic and scientific development of mineral resources in India, as well as to ensure proper utilization and conservation of the nation's mineral wealth.
 
• Nagpur, often referred to as the "Orange City" of India, is a geographically central city and a major trading hub, which makes it a strategic location for the bureau's headquarters.
 
• The city offers connectivity and access to various mining sites across different regions of India.
 
• This central position aids IBM in monitoring, regulation, and enforcement of mining operations efficiently.
 
• The Indian Bureau of Mines has a multifaceted role, including conducting geological surveys, carrying out mineral exploration, and providing technical guidance for the mining sector. It is also involved in the preparation of mineral maps and maintains a repository of mineral resources to facilitate informed decision-making. One of its key functions is regulating and inspecting mines to ensure adherence to safety and environmental standards.
 
• Moreover, IBM is tasked with the responsibility of conducting mineral beneficiation studies and development of mineral processing techniques. It plays a crucial role in advising the central and state governments on all aspects related to mineral wealth and mining legislation. IBM's headquartered location in Nagpur supports its mandate by incorporating research and development initiatives through its various divisions and regional offices.
